questions.question: On a 1:50 000 map, 1 cm on the map represents:
Why does the ratio scale 1:50 000 work with ANY unit of measurement?
options: Because it is unitless — one unit on the map equals 50 000 of the same units on the ground
Because the map legend converts units automatically

questions.question: Which map has the LARGER scale?
8,6 cm on a 1:50 000 map converts to a real distance of:
The correct order of steps is:
options: Measure map distance → multiply by 50 000 → convert cm to m (÷100) → convert m to km (÷1 000)
Convert to km first → multiply by 50 000

questions.question: Why should you show the full unit ladder rather than only using the '× 0,5' shortcut?
options: The memo awards marks for the steps, and the shortcut only works at 1:50 000 while the method works at every scale
The shortcut gives a different answer

questions.question: At 1:50 000, an error of 1 mm in your ruler measurement equals how much real ground?
To measure the distance along a winding road on a map, you should:
options: Use a piece of string or a paper strip along the bends, then straighten it against a ruler
Measure the straight line between the endpoints
Count the contour lines it crosses

questions.question: On a 1:10 000 orthophoto map, 8,6 cm represents:
The real distance is 4,3 km. On a 1:50 000 map the two points are apart by:
options: 8,6 cm — divide the real distance in cm by 50 000

subtopics.title: Verification, Error Traps and Where This Skill Feeds

questions.question: Your calculation of 8,6 cm at 1:50 000 gives 43 km. Which check exposes the error fastest?
options: The sense check: about 10 cm on this map is only 5 km, so 43 km is impossible

questions.question: The metric ladder from centimetres to kilometres is:
Why is rounding 8,6 cm to 9 cm before multiplying a serious error?
options: It introduces a 200 m error in the real distance

questions.question: Which other mapwork calculation directly depends on scale-and-distance as an input?
options: The gradient calculation, which needs the real horizontal distance between the points

subtopics.title: The District, Shrunk Fifty Thousand Times

questions.question: Describing a 1:50 000 map as 'the district shrunk fifty thousand times' tells you that to get back to real ground distance you must:
The cordial rule — one part concentrate to five parts water works in a cup or in a bucket — illustrates which property of a ratio scale?
options: It has no units of its own, so whatever unit you measure with, the answer comes back in that same unit
It applies only to curved distances

questions.question: A 30 cm school ruler laid across a 1:50 000 sheet spans roughly how much real ground?
Why is the divided bar printed along the bottom of a topographic sheet useful?
options: It gives the map's title and sheet number
Its blocks are already labelled in ground distance, so a stepped-off distance can be read without any arithmetic

subtopics.title: Multiply Once, Then Step Down Twice

questions.question: 8,6 cm × 50 000 gives a ground distance of:
Turning 430 000 cm into 4 300 m is like turning cents into rands because:
options: A thousand cents make a rand
A hundred cents make a rand and a hundred centimetres make a metre — so you divide by 100
Money and distance are both measured with rulers

questions.question: Why must the word 'kilometres' be written next to the 4,3?
options: Most memos award a mark for the correct unit, and a bare number forfeits it
It makes the answer look longer

questions.question: The halving shortcut (8,6 × 0,5 = 4,3 km) works on this sheet because:
options: One centimetre on a 1:50 000 map is half a kilometre of ground

subtopics.title: Shoelaces, Zoomed-in Sheets and the Hand-Span Test

questions.question: A shoelace pressed along a winding road measures 12,4 cm on a 1:50 000 map. The real road distance is:
The same 8,6 cm represents only 0,86 km on a 1:10 000 orthophoto rather than 4,3 km because:
options: The orthophoto is the zoomed-in map — a larger scale showing less ground in more detail
The orthophoto was photographed in a different year
Orthophotos may only be measured in metres
The measurement must have been taken incorrectly

questions.question: To turn a real distance of 4,3 km back into a map measurement on a 1:50 000 sheet you should:
options: Convert 4,3 km to 430 000 cm, then divide by 50 000 to get 8,6 cm
Measure the route again with string

questions.question: The hand-span test works because roughly 10 cm of paper on a 1:50 000 sheet is:
options: About 5 km of ground — so an answer of 43 km is instantly impossible
